segments.source: Public goods can benefit many people at once, which creates coordination problems about contributions.
Given facts.

A community project is built only if total voluntary contributions reach 16 tokens. Contributions from 8 households are [1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4]. Everyone can use the project if it is built, including households that contribute zero. Cross-domain check: a survey team starts work at 12:00 and works for 2 hour(s) without a break.
Rules.

Add contributions and compare with the threshold. A public-good threshold concerns whether the project is produced; it does not by itself decide whether every contribution pattern is fair. For the cross-domain check, finishing time = starting time + duration.
Task.
Is the project built? How many additional tokens, if any, are needed? Cross-domain check: at what time does the team finish?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Total contribution=1+2+3+4+1+2+3+4=20. 2. Compare 20 with threshold 16. 3. Additional amount needed=max(0,16−20)=0. Cross-domain check: 12+2=14, so the team finishes at 14:00.
Answer.
The project is built. Additional tokens needed: 0. Cross-domain answer: 14:00.
Knowledge takeaway.
Threshold provision and fairness are separate questions; first determine whether enough resources exist.
Formal model.
Sum contributions; compare with provision threshold; compute shortfall.
N19. Common resources and avoiding depletion
Problem 966. Using a shared renewable resource: case 1
Knowledge context.
A common resource can be overused when many individually reasonable withdrawals add up to more than regeneration.
Given facts.

A shared fishery has 100 fish at the start of the period and regenerates 10. There are 7 users, each planning to take 3. For this simplified exercise, the stock should not decline below its starting level if use is to be called non-depleting.
Rules.
End stock = start + regeneration − total harvest. Total harvest is number of users × harvest per user.
Task.
What is the end stock? Is the planned use non-depleting under the stated definition? What equal per-user harvest would exactly match regeneration?
Step-by-step solution.
1. Total harvest=7×3=21. 2. End stock=100+10−21=89. 3. To match regeneration exactly, equal harvest per user would be 10÷7=1.43.
Answer.
End stock 89; depleting. Equal regeneration-matching share: 1.43 each.
Knowledge takeaway.
The shared-resource problem appears at the total level, so individual plans must be aggregated.
Formal model.
Commons stock equation plus equal-share benchmark.
